title: Use a colon for hierarchical descent in artifact names

values: an artifact identifier steps from a more general conceptual level to a more specific one (hierarchical descent) and a separator must be chosen or checked at that step
facts.note: Sufficient on its own to activate. Whether adjacent name segments are different conceptual levels (general->specific) is a semantic judgement; no mechanical observer exists.
Illustrative cue only, not a gate: authoring, renaming or reviewing an artifact identifier.
Illustrative cue only, not a gate: the rule applies to any hierarchy-naming task even when none of these terms appear.

fires: Planner names an artifact whose identifier descends from a theme/domain into a subsystem/collection, then a category/type, then an item/entity.
Planner renames an artifact identifier and must choose the separator between a parent level and the child level beneath it.
Planner or reviewer checks an existing or planned identifier where a deeper, more specific level is joined to its parent.
doesNotFire: Joining words that are on the same conceptual level (e.g. a multi-word name of a single segment) — separator semantics for that case are governed by the related separator-semantics rule.
Work that does not author, rename or review an artifact identifier.
Free-form prose in plan docs that is not an artifact identifier.

given: A planner is composing, renaming or reviewing an artifact identifier whose segments span different conceptual levels of the resource tree
when: choosing or checking the separator where the identifier descends from a more general level to a more specific one
then: Use a colon for that hierarchical descent: join the general level and the more specific level beneath it with a colon (general->specific, navigating deeper through organizational subsystems).
prefer: Order segments from general to specific, joined by colons, e.g. commons:ux:foundations:color (theme->subsystem->category->item).
Use colons for organizational subsystems and collections as you navigate deeper, e.g. scenario:catalog:primitives:actor (domain->collection->type->entity).
avoid: Using a colon between parts that sit on the same conceptual level, which falsely signals descent.
Using another separator (dot, dash, underscore) to step down a level, which hides the hierarchy.
why: Hierarchical descent means moving from general to specific down the resource tree, and that movement is marked by a colon.
evidence: Where the planned identifier steps from a parent level to a more specific child level (different conceptual levels), that step is joined by a colon.
Reading the colon-joined levels left to right yields a general->specific path such as theme->subsystem->category->item or domain->collection->type->entity.
verifier_detail: Term hierarchical_descent: moving from general to specific down the resource tree, marked by a colon.
Colon signals: different conceptual levels, navigating deeper, general->specific, organizational subsystems.
No mechanical detector: level distinction is LLM-judged; implementation and fix_hint were not preserved from legacy source.
